messages:
Anya: Quick RFC follow-up — during the perf test with 50 tenants we saw egress failures for private endpoints. Root cause looks like MTU fragmentation + per-account peering route limits. Anyone else hit this?

Matt: saw it. lots of tcp retransmits + ENOBUFS. Changing `tcp_mtu_probe` didn't help. :grimacing:

Sofia: can you paste logs? which path — regional relay -> customer VPC peering or private endpoint through gw?

Anya: Relay -> peering. Logs snippet: `error: route add failed: RTNETLINK answers: File exists` and `fragmentation needed but DF set` — plus a few `ICMP frag needed` messages in the relay kernel.

Kevin: sounds like two separate constraints colliding. AWS peering route limit per route table (~1000) was hit when we created per-tenant /28s. We also saw PMTU issues from GRE/UDP encapsulation on relay -> customer path. Options: reduce per-tenant prefix granularity, use ENI-based NAT at the relay, or move to PrivateLink.

Priya: tradeoffs: PrivateLink avoids route explosion and peering quotas but introduces per-connection ENI limits and higher egress cost. Also you lose full-route visibility unless we instrument the proxy.

Raj: sketched a hybrid approach: keep regional relay for latency-critical paths, but publish aggregated prefixes per customer (eg. one /24) and NAT inside relay to preserve tenant IPs. That reduces route count and avoids per-tenant route churn.

Anya: sketch please.

Raj: here is a small terraform sketch for aggregated routes we used in the spike:
```
resource "aws_route" "tenant_agg" {
  route_table_id           = aws_route_table.customer_rt.id
  destination_cidr_block   = "10.${var.tenant_id}.0.0/24"
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.relay.id
}
```

Matt: Aggregation reduces route count but forces NAT/masq at the relay which breaks the zero-NAT tenant model. Ops surface increases (ipam, SNAT elasticity). Also need to watch connection tracking.

Priya: also run SLA/cost analysis — PrivateLink pilot will increase egress $/GB by ~3x for that path, but reduces operational complexity. Might be worth for high-SLO customers.

infra-bot: perf-test-2026-03-10 finished. failures: 12/50 tenants failed egress, 9 peering route errors, 7 MTU-related retransmit spikes. Full report: https://redwood.internal/reports/pex374

Anya: Proposal action items — short-term (hotfix): implement MTU clamp on relay (tcp_mss/tcp_mtu_probing) + aggregated prefixes + relay NAT; medium-term: pilot PrivateLink for 5 highest-SLO customers; long-term: design ENI-per-tenant / virtual interface model in Dedicated to avoid NAT.

Sofia: +1. Need canary rollout plan, test checklist, and a retro doc. Who will own infra changes?

Kevin: I'll own the short-term MTU and NAT patch. Raj will prototype aggregated prefix NAT and run perf-tests. Priya will own cost model and PrivateLink pilot plan. Anya will file RFC follow-up and coordinate canary dates.

Anya: Thanks all — I'll open the RFC follow-up and add the checklist. Meeting to sync on Monday 10:30 PT. :sparkles:
